hook: Bo the bear cub shows the five cues of an underhand or overhand throw, then the class runs a real throwing test: soft balls at a paper target taped on the wall beside the screen, one way and then another, while the board stacks every hit in ten-frames and the class sees which way hits more.
outcome: Throw underhand and overhand with the key cues (face the target, arm back, step with the opposite foot, release, follow through), and run a fair test that compares two ways of throwing by counting hits
sources: SHAPE America, National Physical Education Standards (2024), Standard 1: https://www.shapeamerica.org/standards/pe/

Underhand and overhand throw critical elements: SHAPE America, National Standards & Grade-Level Outcomes for K-12 Physical Education (Human Kinetics, 2014), outcomes S1.E13 and S1.E14, and the matching rubrics in PE Metrics, 3rd ed. (SHAPE America, Human Kinetics, 2019)
Soft equipment and safe spacing: SHAPE America, Appropriate Instructional Practice Guidelines, K-12 (2009): https://www.shapeamerica.org/standards/guidelines/
Fair test (change one thing, keep the rest the same): NGSS Science and Engineering Practice 3, Planning and Carrying Out Investigations (K-2 grade band)
Bo, the target, the ten-frames and the icons are drawn in code; the sounds are generated in the browser
